open_points.subject: Viewer access-link issuance and use
open_points.text: “authenticates through an unguessable capability link (`ViewerAccessCredential`) issued and re-issuable by an operator” and “a successful entry opens a managed `ViewerSession`”
open_points.question: What exactly does issuance return, who receives that one-time secret or URL, and may the same link be used repeatedly to create additional sessions until revoked, or is it consumed on first entry?
options: Return a full link once and allow repeated entries until revocation
Return a secret once and consume it on first successful entry
Return an identifier and rely on a separate delivery operation
open_points.default_guess: Return the full link once and allow repeated entries until it is revoked or re-issued.

witness.initial: A viewer has a newly issued credential and no session.
events: The administrator gives the link to the viewer.
The viewer enters successfully and receives a session cookie.
The viewer opens the same link in another browser.
outcomes: A second viewer session is created because the credential remains valid.
Entry is rejected because the credential was consumed by the first use.

open_points.subject: ClientViewer identity record
open_points.text: “A permanent read-only viewer identity representing one client” and “created by an operator”
open_points.question: Which identifying inputs and stored facts create a ClientViewer, and what prevents or permits multiple viewer records for the same real client?
options: Only an opaque viewer ID is required and duplicates are allowed
A required display name or external client reference identifies the viewer
A Registry-owned client identifier provides uniqueness
open_points.default_guess: Require a portal display name, assign an opaque viewer ID, and allow administrators to decide whether separate records represent the same person.

witness.initial: No viewer exists for a client who owns two projects.
events: An administrator creates a viewer for the first project.
Later another administrator onboards the same client for the second project.
outcomes: The second administrator finds and grants the existing viewer.
A second unrelated viewer identity is created because no lookup or uniqueness fact is defined.

open_points.subject: Staff account lifecycle
open_points.text: “suspending or disabling an account invalidates its active sessions”; R0-14 also names “revoking” staff accounts, while R0-19 uses `pending_verification` and `active`
open_points.question: What is the closed StaffAccount status set, which transitions are allowed, and are suspend, disable, and revoke distinct states or names for the same operation?
options: `pending_verification`, `active`, `suspended`, and `disabled` are distinct states
Suspend is reversible and disable/revoke is permanent
All three terms mean one inactive status
open_points.default_guess: Use distinct pending, active, suspended, and disabled states; treat revocation as transition to disabled.

witness.initial: A logged-in active operator has assigned projects.
events: An administrator suspends the account.
A different administrator later tries to revoke or disable it.
The original operator attempts to log in again.
outcomes: Suspension is reversible, while disable/revoke is a distinct permanent transition.
All terms target the same inactive state and reactivation has one common behavior.

open_points.subject: Administrator project mutations
open_points.text: “Operators hold mutation capabilities for their assigned projects. Administrators additionally hold access-management capabilities” versus “a human operator/administrator reviews and activates”
open_points.question: May an administrator perform budget, expense, progress, payment, photo, and activation mutations by virtue of the administrator role, or only when the administrator also has an assignment to that project?
options: Administrators may mutate every project in their administrative area
Administrators need the same project assignment as operators
Administrators may activate imports globally but need assignments for other mutations
open_points.default_guess: Require administrators to have a project assignment for ordinary project mutations, including activation.

witness.initial: An administrator is not assigned to project P, which has an imported snapshot awaiting activation.
events: The administrator opens P and attempts to activate the snapshot.
outcomes: Activation succeeds because administrators have project-wide operational authority.
Activation is denied because project assignment is required in addition to role capability.

open_points.subject: Service credential rotation
open_points.text: “rotatable with an overlap period”
open_points.question: Who chooses the overlap duration, what bounds or default apply, and does the old credential expire automatically at the end of that period?
options: A fixed configured overlap automatically expires the old credential
The administrator supplies a bounded overlap duration
Both credentials remain valid until the old one is explicitly revoked
open_points.default_guess: Use a deployment-configured overlap and automatically revoke the old credential when it ends.

witness.initial: A producer has credential A.
events: An administrator rotates A and receives credential B.
The producer continues using A after the unspecified overlap time.
outcomes: A is automatically rejected after a defined deadline.
A remains valid until an administrator explicitly revokes it.

open_points.subject: Viewer session restoration
open_points.text: “Viewers can restore and end their session explicitly.”
open_points.question: What does “restore” mean, what input authorizes it, and what observable result or failure does the action have?
options: Re-entering a still-valid access link creates a new session
A refresh token renews the existing session without sliding its fixed expiry
The browser merely checks and resumes an existing cookie-backed session
open_points.default_guess: Treat restoration as re-entering a valid access link to create a new fixed-expiry session.

witness.initial: A viewer's browser cookie is gone, but the access link has not been revoked.
events: The viewer invokes the documented restore action.
outcomes: A new session is created using the access-link credential.
Restoration fails because it requires an existing session cookie.

open_points.subject: Initial staff-password handoff
open_points.text: “The administrator hands the initial password to the holder outside the portal: no portal operation, message or answer carries it.”
open_points.question: What actor or external channel performs this necessary handoff, what minimum authenticity/confidentiality assumptions apply, and what happens when delivery fails or reaches the wrong person?
options: The organization owns an explicitly out-of-band secure handoff with no portal tracking
The administrator chooses any channel and assumes delivery
The account remains pending until the holder acknowledges receipt through a named external process
open_points.default_guess: Make the organization responsible for a confidential, identity-checked out-of-band handoff and keep the account pending until the administrator confirms it.

witness.initial: An administrator creates a pending account with an initial password.
events: The administrator sends the password through an unspecified outside channel.
The administrator activates the account.
Someone attempts login with the password.
outcomes: The intended holder received it and gains access.
A wrong recipient received it and gains access; the portal has no delivery fact or failure to distinguish the histories.
witness.observer: The intended holder, administrator, and security auditor

open_points.subject: Initial password change
open_points.text: “the holder logs in with the initial password and changes it”
open_points.question: Is changing the initial password mandatory before any other operation, merely recommended, or not represented in product state?
options: First login is restricted to changing the password
The initial password has a deadline but normal access is otherwise allowed
Changing it is optional
open_points.default_guess: Require a password change immediately after the first successful login before granting normal capabilities.

witness.initial: An activated operator has never changed the administrator-selected initial password.
events: The operator logs in.
The operator attempts to create an expense without changing the password.
outcomes: The mutation is blocked until the password is changed.
The mutation succeeds because the text describes only an expected user action.

open_points.subject: Bootstrap command interface
open_points.text: “the email and password are its inputs, read neither from process arguments nor from the environment nor from a file” and “Its outcome is a closed set of exit codes”
open_points.question: How does the command receive the email and password, and what are the exact exit codes and meanings for success, existing staff, invalid input, configuration failure, and persistence failure?
options: Read both through an interactive TTY and publish distinct documented exit codes
Read them from standard input and use one generic nonzero failure code
Use an operating-system credential channel and structured exit statuses
open_points.default_guess: Prompt on a controlling TTY with hidden password entry and define distinct stable exit codes for success, already initialized, invalid input, configuration failure, and storage failure.

witness.initial: A deployment has no staff accounts and an automation invokes the bootstrap command without a TTY.
events: The automation supplies no argv, environment variable, or file because all are forbidden.
The command needs the two required inputs.
outcomes: The command reads a documented stdin protocol and succeeds.
The command requires an interactive TTY and fails with an implementation-chosen exit code.
witness.observer: The host operator and deployment script

open_points.subject: Bootstrap audit provenance
open_points.text: R0-07 says the first-administrator command is “never printed, logged or audited,” while Primary outcomes says “Every significant action records actor provenance” and includes access-management actions
open_points.question: Is creation of the first administrator exempt from the universal audit promise, or must a non-secret bootstrap audit record be created, and if so what actor provenance identifies the host action?
options: Bootstrap is explicitly exempt and produces no audit record
Bootstrap creates an audit record attributed to a host/bootstrap actor
Bootstrap writes a separate host audit outside the portal database
open_points.default_guess: Create a non-secret audit record attributed to a bootstrap host actor.

witness.initial: The deployment has no staff accounts.
events: A host operator runs the bootstrap command successfully.
An auditor later inspects the portal's complete significant-action history.
outcomes: No record of the first administrator's creation exists, as R0-07 requires.
A creation record exists, as the universal audit outcome requires.

open_points.subject: Password reset availability
open_points.text: R0-06 is titled “Sessions, self-service reset” and says a staff member may request a password reset, while R0-23 says the request “does nothing” and completing a reset returns a concealed rejection
open_points.question: For the product that later agents must implement, is self-service password reset an available outcome or an intentionally unavailable deferred feature?
options: Implement the full reset flow described by R0-06
Expose inert request/completion operations exactly as R0-23 says
Do not expose reset operations until Q19 is resolved
open_points.default_guess: Implement the accepted current behavior: expose inert operations, while explicitly marking self-service reset unavailable.

witness.initial: An active staff member has access to their verified email but has forgotten the password.
events: The staff member requests a reset.
The staff member waits for a token and attempts completion.
outcomes: A reset token is delivered and the password can be changed under R0-06's self-service-reset decision.
Nothing is delivered and completion is rejected under R0-23.

open_points.subject: Authority of deferred challenge operations
open_points.text: R0-15 says email verification, email-change confirmation, and password-reset completion “Each of them proves its own authority … [with] a single-use token,” while R0-23 says those operations read nothing and reject without carrying out challenges
open_points.question: Must these unauthenticated operations validate a token now, or must they remain unconditional inert rejections until Q19 is built?
options: Validate tokens and perform the corresponding operation
Reject every call without reading or validating a token
Remove the routes until challenge support exists
open_points.default_guess: Keep the routes inert and reject without token validation, matching R0-23's accepted-service behavior.

witness.initial: A caller submits a syntactically valid confirmation token to an unauthenticated confirmation operation.
events: The portal receives the request.
outcomes: The portal validates the single-use token as the operation's authority under R0-15.
The portal reads nothing and returns the concealed rejection under R0-23.

open_points.subject: Sole-administrator recovery
open_points.text: “No product operation recovers a sole administrator who has lost both password and email … such a recovery stays a host-level operation outside the product”
open_points.question: What host-level actor and operation perform that recovery, what facts may they change, and is the same operation available when only the password is lost while R0-23 leaves password reset inert?
options: A documented host command resets email and/or password with host audit
A database administrator edits storage directly
There is deliberately no supported recovery until email challenges are implemented
open_points.default_guess: Provide a separate host-only recovery command that can replace email and password and emits a host-level audit record.

witness.initial: The only administrator forgets the password but still controls the login email.
events: The administrator requests a password reset, which does nothing under R0-23.
The host operator seeks the recovery described in R0-20.
outcomes: The host-level recovery applies to password-only loss and restores access.
Recovery is defined only for loss of both password and email, leaving the deployment permanently locked out.
witness.observer: The sole administrator and host operator

open_points.subject: Health checks
open_points.text: “The service answers an unauthenticated liveness and readiness check”
open_points.question: What exact HTTP statuses and response shapes represent live, ready, and not ready, and which dependency or startup conditions make readiness fail?
options: Both return fixed JSON; liveness tests the process and readiness tests database plus binary-root access
Both return empty responses and readiness only means startup completed
Readiness also calls Registry and fails when Registry is unavailable
open_points.default_guess: Return minimal fixed JSON; liveness reports process health, while readiness requires validated configuration, open SQLite access, and accessible binary storage but not Registry availability.

witness.initial: The service process is running, SQLite is accessible, and Registry is unavailable.
events: An orchestrator calls liveness.
The orchestrator calls readiness.
outcomes: Readiness succeeds because external Registry availability is not a local readiness dependency.
Readiness fails because project operations depend on Registry.

open_points.subject: Concealed binary-read failure
open_points.text: “An unknown, cross-project, hidden, oversize or unlisted read is answered the same way”
open_points.question: What is that single response's HTTP status, body, headers, and audit behavior?
options: A bodyless 404 for every concealed case
A bodyless 403 for every concealed case
A generic JSON error with one status for every concealed case
open_points.default_guess: Return a bodyless 404 with no object-derived headers and audit authenticated denied attempts without recording secrets.

witness.initial: A viewer is authenticated for project A.
events: The viewer requests a nonexistent document ID.
The viewer requests a real document belonging to project B.
outcomes: Both requests return the same bodyless 404.
Both return the same generic 403 or JSON error selected by another implementer.
witness.observer: The viewer client and API integrator

open_points.subject: Snapshot import response
open_points.text: “A producer reads an earlier import result by its `import_id`”
open_points.question: How is `import_id` created and returned by the import action, and does import return the completed result synchronously, an accepted/pending result, or both an immediate result and a later lookup handle?
options: Import completes synchronously and returns `import_id` plus the final result
Import returns `import_id` with pending status for later lookup
The producer supplies an idempotency/import identifier
open_points.default_guess: Have the portal create and return `import_id` together with a final synchronous import result.

witness.initial: An authorized producer has a valid snapshot and no prior import.
events: The producer submits the snapshot.
The connection closes after the server commits but before the producer receives the full response.
The producer wants to query the import result.
outcomes: The producer already chose or can deterministically recover the import ID and queries safely.
Only the lost response contained a server-generated import ID, so the producer cannot use R0-21.

open_points.subject: Snapshot rejection response
open_points.text: “Client Portal validates and imports the exact version” and rejected imports record “rejection reasons”
open_points.question: Which validation failures are distinguishable to the producer, whether a rejected attempt receives and persists an `import_id`, and what result is returned for malformed contracts, unauthorized projects, foreign currency, duplicate conflicts, and unsupported versions are not stated.
options: Every authenticated attempt creates an import result with typed rejection reasons
Only structurally valid attempts create import records; earlier failures are generic errors
Authorization failures are concealed while business validation failures are typed and persisted
open_points.default_guess: Conceal authorization failures, but persist and return typed import results for authenticated business and integrity validation failures.

witness.initial: A producer is allowed for project P and has already imported snapshot version V.
events: The producer resubmits V with different content.
The producer asks for the attempt's result.
outcomes: The conflict creates a retrievable rejected import result with its own `import_id`.
The request returns an immediate error and creates no import result.

open_points.subject: Registry project context
open_points.text: “Sole owner of project identity and current context” and the client sees “Registry project context”
open_points.question: Which Registry context fields are consumed and exposed to clients, and how are absent, newly added, sensitive, or unsupported fields handled?
options: Expose a closed portal-owned projection of named Registry fields
Proxy the complete Registry context response
Store and expose a snapshot captured when the grant or write was made
open_points.default_guess: Define and expose a closed portal-owned projection fetched from Registry at read time.

witness.initial: Registry returns a project context containing a name, address, internal note, and owner metadata.
events: A viewer opens the project.
outcomes: Only a closed safe projection such as name and address is returned.
The complete Registry context, including the internal note, is returned because “project context” was left abstract.

open_points.subject: Registry failure during reads
open_points.text: “Every project-scoped operation checks … Registry project lifecycle policy” and “Unavailable data is shown explicitly”
open_points.question: When Registry is unavailable, times out, returns an unknown status, or reports a granted project missing, does the portal fail the whole request, omit that project, return partial data with explicit unavailability, or use cached context?
options: Fail the affected request with a typed dependency error
Return portal-owned data with Registry context marked unavailable
Use last-known Registry status and context
Omit unavailable projects from lists
open_points.default_guess: Fail mutations closed; for reads, return portal-owned data only if lifecycle status can still be established safely, otherwise return a typed dependency-unavailable error.

witness.initial: A viewer has a valid grant to project P and portal-owned budget data; Registry is down.
events: The viewer lists projects.
The viewer opens P.
outcomes: Both requests fail because lifecycle authorization cannot be checked.
P and its portal data are returned with Registry context explicitly unavailable.

open_points.subject: Confirmed OCR result contract
open_points.text: “confirmed normalized recognition result … supported `contract_version`, complete confirmed content”
open_points.question: What fields constitute complete confirmed content, their types and requiredness, and the validation and failure behavior for unsupported versions, missing fields, invalid totals, or a conflicting replay are not named.
options: Define a closed versioned schema in this state
Treat normalized content as an opaque payload preserved by the portal
Defer the schema but explicitly name the fields the Expense model consumes
open_points.default_guess: Define a closed versioned schema containing the recognized-document identity, document date/reference, supplier, gross EUR total, and provenance reference, with typed validation failures.

witness.initial: An operator submits a confirmed result containing a document ID and total but no supplier or document date.
events: The portal validates the claimed complete content.
outcomes: The expense is accepted because those fields are optional or irrelevant.
The expense is rejected because they are required parts of complete content.
witness.observer: The operator and OCR adapter implementer

open_points.subject: Prepared progress-photo facts
open_points.text: “It consumes … prepared photo facts from Telegram intake” and “a progress photo is published the same way”
open_points.question: What facts comprise a prepared photo submission, which are supplied by intake versus staff, and which validation failures prevent publication?
options: A closed contract includes `file_ref`, provenance reference, capture time, media type, caption, section and visibility
Only `file_ref` and provenance come from intake; all display facts come from staff
The portal accepts an opaque prepared-facts object
open_points.default_guess: Require `file_ref`, provenance reference, and capture time from intake, with caption, section association, and visibility explicitly supplied by authenticated staff.

witness.initial: A binary exists with a file reference but has no capture timestamp.
events: An operator submits it as a progress photo.
A viewer opens the chronological gallery.
outcomes: Publication is rejected because chronological ordering requires a capture-time fact.
Publication succeeds and the portal uses publication time as the chronology fact.

open_points.subject: Expense replay conflict
open_points.text: “One recognized document creates at most one Expense with one Document; replay is idempotent.”
open_points.question: What happens when the same `recognized_document_id` is replayed with different recognized content, project selection, inclusion state, or allocation, and is the identity global or scoped to a project?
options: Exact replay returns the original result; any difference is an integrity conflict
Every replay returns the existing expense and ignores differences
The ID is scoped per project, allowing the same ID in different projects
open_points.default_guess: Make `recognized_document_id` globally unique; exact replay returns the original result and any changed content, project, or allocation is an integrity conflict.

witness.initial: Recognition ID R already created an expense in project A allocated to section X.
events: An operator submits R again for project B with a different total and allocation.
outcomes: The portal rejects an integrity conflict and leaves the original unchanged.
The portal idempotently returns the original expense, silently ignoring the conflicting request.

open_points.subject: Payment replay conflict
open_points.text: “register work payments (idempotent by stable payment identity)”
open_points.question: Who supplies the stable payment identity, what is its uniqueness scope, and what happens when the same identity is replayed with a different amount, date, project, or provenance?
options: Caller-supplied globally unique identity with conflict-on-difference
Caller-supplied identity unique only within one project
Portal-generated identity, with idempotency provided by a separate request key
Replay always returns the existing payment and ignores differences
open_points.default_guess: Use a caller-supplied identity unique within a project; exact replay returns the original payment and different content conflicts.

witness.initial: Payment ID M exists in project P for EUR 1,000.
events: An operator retries M for EUR 1,100 after an uncertain response.
outcomes: The portal rejects a content conflict.
The portal returns the existing EUR 1,000 payment as an idempotent success without exposing the mismatch.

open_points.subject: Progress editing on imported budgets
open_points.text: “update manual work progress per section (0–100%)”
open_points.question: Does “manual” describe staff-entered progress for every active budget source, or restrict progress updates to manual-budget sections?
options: Staff may enter progress for sections of either active budget source
Progress is editable only for manual budgets
Imported snapshots require progress from another external source
open_points.default_guess: Treat “manual” as the entry method and permit updates for sections of either active budget source.

witness.initial: Project P has an active imported snapshot with a work-planned section.
events: An assigned operator attempts to set that section to 50% complete.
outcomes: The update succeeds because progress is manually entered for all sections.
The update is denied because only manual-budget sections support manual progress.

open_points.subject: Work progress across budget-version changes
open_points.text: The transition rules preserve and map expenses and say “payments and photos do not depend on budget version changes,” but do not say what happens to “work progress per section.”
open_points.question: When a new budget version is activated, is existing section progress mapped by stable section identity, retained only with the inactive version, reset, or blocked pending explicit mapping?
options: Map progress automatically for matching stable section IDs and require manual decisions for the rest
Keep progress version-specific and show only progress entered for the active version
Reset all progress on activation
Block activation until every progress record is mapped
open_points.default_guess: Carry progress across matching stable section identities and require explicit mapping for nonmatching sections without resetting history.

witness.initial: Section S in the active manual budget is 60% complete; an imported version contains the same stable section identity.
events: An operator activates the imported version.
A viewer opens project progress.
outcomes: S remains 60% complete through stable-identity mapping.
The imported section has unavailable or 0% progress because progress is version-specific or reset.

open_points.subject: Activation with unmapped allocations
open_points.text: “existing allocations require explicit mapping to the sections of the newly activated version” but “unmapped expenses stay visible and must be resolved by an operator”
open_points.question: May a budget version be activated while allocations remain unmapped, or must all mapping decisions be complete before activation?
options: Activation is allowed and unmapped allocations enter an explicit unresolved state
Activation is blocked until every existing allocation is mapped
Only exact stable-ID matches are required before activation; other allocations may remain unresolved
open_points.default_guess: Allow activation with an explicit unresolved allocation state, because the text promises unmapped expenses remain visible for later resolution.

witness.initial: A project has an expense allocated to a manual section with no stable counterpart in an imported version.
events: An operator attempts to activate the imported version without choosing a manual mapping.
outcomes: Activation succeeds and the expense appears as unresolved/unmapped.
Activation fails because existing allocations require explicit mapping before the version can become active.

open_points.subject: Actual-materials calculation
open_points.text: “Actual materials” and “only confirmed included expenses join financial totals”
open_points.question: Is actual materials the sum of included allocation amounts per active section and `Other expenses`, how are allocations mapped across versions treated, and are unresolved allocations included in project totals but excluded from section totals?
options: Sum included allocations; unresolved amounts count only in the project total
Exclude unresolved allocations from every actual-materials total
Use each included expense total independently of allocation state
open_points.default_guess: Sum confirmed included allocation amounts; count unresolved amounts in a separately disclosed project-level bucket but not in any section total.

witness.initial: An included EUR 100 expense survives a budget change but its allocation is unmapped.
events: A viewer reads project and section actual-material totals.
outcomes: The project total includes EUR 100 while section totals exclude it and disclose it as unresolved.
The EUR 100 is absent from actual-material totals until mapping is resolved.

open_points.subject: Audit failure scope
open_points.text: “Every significant action records … result” while R0-23 says deferred challenge operations “audit … nothing”
open_points.question: Which rejected, unauthorized, validation-failed, and inert requests count as significant actions and receive audit records, and which are intentionally excluded?
options: Audit every authenticated command attempt and security-sensitive unauthenticated attempt
Audit only successful state changes plus explicitly listed import rejections
Audit successful and business-rejected actions but not authentication failures or inert routes
open_points.default_guess: Audit authenticated command attempts and security-sensitive authentication/revocation failures, while exempting health checks and the explicitly inert deferred challenge routes.

witness.initial: An authenticated operator attempts an expense change on an unassigned project.
events: Authorization rejects the request.
An auditor searches for the attempt.
outcomes: An audit record exists with denied result because the significant action was attempted.
No audit record exists because no business state changed.
